full_judgment: (a) when the Constitutionality of a law is challenged the Court is to begin with the presumption of constitutionality of the law (East Pakistan V. Serajul Haque, 19 DLR(SC)281). The person challenging the validity of the law must show that the law is clearly unconstitutional (Home Tel & Tel co. V. Loss Angels, 211 US 265 and Madhubhai Bhandi V. India, AIR 1961 SC 21). In case of reasonable doubt as to whether the law is unconstitutional, the Court will resolve the doubt in favour of constitutionality of the law (Cooley, Constitutional Limitations, 1927).
